In the background, Survivor recounts panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died and Lone holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy murder trial speaks out keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Duncan Sheik, singer and composer of Spring Awakening, dies at 56
headlines.description: The musician, who went from 90s alt-pop hits to Tony-winning Broadway success, died from cardiac arrest Duncan Sheik, the singer-songwriter behind the 90s alt-pop touchstone Barely Breathing and the composer of the Tony -winning musical Spring Awakening, died on Thursday at a Manhattan hospital. He was 56. His death, from heart failure that led to cardiac arrest, was confirmed to the New York Times by his mother Suzanne Sheik.

headlines.title: Early voting begins in midterms as campaign shifts focus to cost of living and Iran war – US politics live
headlines.description: Campaigning or control of Congress is expected to ramp up as some states open early voting Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, announced at a news conference today plans for tighter rules on data center development in order to address transparency, energy use and environmental concerns. And Nevada’s governor, Joe Lombardo, a Republican, signed an executive order aimed at tackling similar issues.

headlines.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
headlines.description: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?

headlines.title: Survivor recounts panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died
headlines.description: Police fire teargas as protests break out in the city of Minna after the deaths of the suspected illegal goldminers A survivor from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group has recounted his panic and struggle for breath, as police fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths earlier this week. Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) – a paramilitary group that works with police – initially blamed the deaths in Minna, the state capital of mineral-rich Niger state, on a disease outbreak.

headlines.title: Lone holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy murder trial speaks out
headlines.description: Michael P Desronvil was sole juror to vote guilty, resulting in deadlocked jury and judge declaring a mistrial Ron DeSantis offers ‘asylum’ to holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial The lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial is speaking out, saying that he “didn’t have any doubts” during the jury’s deliberations of the case which ended in a mistrial. “I didn’t have any doubts. As I tried to explain different possible theories during deliberation, I kept getting cut off as if I had doubts based on the evidence present,” the 48-year-old male juror, Michael P Desronvil, said in a statement to NewsNation on Thursday.

headlines.description: Authorities linked the deaths to disease, but this has been disputed by intelligence reports and relatives of the accused.

headlinePool.title: Flight chaos for hundreds of thousands was caused in ‘millisecond’ by software error
headlinePool.description: Error first occurred at 10am but major incident was not declared until 12.30pm, says report Business live – latest updates A software defect in part of the UK’s air traffic control system corrupted flight data “in the space of a millisecond”, leading to a six-hour outage and mass airline cancellations and delays across the UK last week, National Air Traffic Services has said. But ministers said the Nats report into the incident still left questions unanswered, saying they needed “to urgently understand why this issue was not discovered and fixed before it caused chaos”.

headlinePool.title: Marks and Spencer’s first LFW catwalk gamble pays off with compelling looks at affordable prices
headlinePool.description: Retailer’s message is ‘fashion with a small f’ as it picks up on trends and brings styles for everyone to debut runway show Joan Collins declared the coats “very chic”, and has her eye on a graceful ivory evening dress with caped shoulders. Kemi Badenoch plans to snap up the classic black tuxedo jacket. If the British public are as enthusiastic as the celebrity front row, Marks & Spencer’s first ever London fashion week catwalk looks like a hit. The show, held at the Design Museum for 310 guests including Ian Wright and Jamie Carragher, was a gamble on both sides. Would snobby fashionistas be traumatised by elasticated waistbands and practical rainwear? Would M&S customers be alienated by a world of £2,000 handbags and shoes you can’t walk in?

headlinePool.title: Reform donor Ben Delo loaned £350k to academic found to have engaged in online bullying
headlinePool.description: Judge said Nina Power and her friend’s social media posts had ‘the whiff of threat and antisemitism’ Reform UK’s new mega-donor Ben Delo gave a £350,000 loan to a conservative writer fighting a legal case in which a judge later found she had engaged in online bullying and regrettable conduct with a “whiff of threat and antisemitism”. Nina Power and her friend, the writer Daniel DC Miller, brought the legal action for defamation against the performance artist Luke Turner, who they had accused of falsely calling them antisemitic. At the same time, Turner brought a counter-claim against the pair accusing them of harassment.

headlinePool.title: Burnham urged by opposition parties to follow Macron and act with more urgency on Russian threat – as it happened
headlinePool.description: French president Emmanuel Macron earlier said he put measures in place to protect the country’s critical infrastructure Micheál Martin , the taoiseach (Irish PM), thanked Andy Burnham for his stance on Israel as the two men met at No 10 North today. Support for the Palestinian cause is particularly strong in Ireland because of its historical experience of colonialism, and, in a reference to the sanctions on West Bank settlements imposed by Burnham’s government, Martin said: I think for the United Kingdom under your leadership to take the stance that it’s taken, I think, is important for … standing up for humanitarian values and justice and fulfilling the rights of all in the Middle East to security, to peace and to some decent future for their children and generations to come. Formed in 1999, the UK Youth Parliament (UKYP) sees more than 300 children aged 11 to 18 democratically elected by their peers to represent young people in their area, who then debate and campaign on a variety of issues. Once a year, they hold a debate in the House of Commons chamber.

headlinePool.description: The French president says he has tasked the government with protecting critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.

headlinePool.title: At least 17 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
headlinePool.description: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.

headlinePool.title: Diana book sparks royal row between King Charles and Earl Spencer - The Latest
headlinePool.description: Buckingham Palace has issued a rare, and strong, rebuttal to claims made in Earl Spencer’s memoir Swan Song. The book claims that King Charles told Spencer days after Diana’s death and during a heated row over funeral arrangements: ‘Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.’ Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s senior national news editor, Aaron Sharp

headlinePool.title: Alleged underworld supporters and unfounded health claims: One Nation rolls out more Victorian election candidates
headlinePool.description: Party has unveiled a steady stream of contenders for state election, including a former councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving Pauline Hanson announced who would be her party’s upper house candidates and Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, at a press conference last month . Since then One Nation has used social media to unveil a steady stream of candidates, with 51 of the 88 lower house spots now filled.

headlinePool.title: Swedish teenager jailed for attempted murder, rape and assault committed online, with victims in Germany and Australia
headlinePool.description: Eighteen-year-old known as Chai was active in networks notorious for their sadistic exploitation of young people A Swedish teenager known as Chai has been sentenced to more than 10 years in jail for attempted murder, rape and aggravated assault – crimes committed via the internet, including against a teenage girl in Australia . The district court found that Chai, 18, was active in online networks notorious for their sadistic extortion of young and vulnerable people, coercing them to create sexually explicit material or engage in acts of violence – and for the youth of those involved. In Australia, support is available at Beyond Blue on 1300 22 4636, Lifeline on 13 11 14, and at MensLine on 1300 789 978. In the UK, the charity Mind is available on 0300 123 3393 and Childline on 0800 1111. In the US, call or text Mental Health America at 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.
